sourceAnchors.visualArbitrationNote: Table 13 is visually legible on printed page 172. It arranges characterological Mitte variations as joint e/hy/k/p configurations and gives examples for socialization and pathology. The table is retained as a reference map rather than decomposed into row-level doctrine.
Printed page 173 introduces Table 14 as the important variations of the Mitte across the source's historical Trieberkrankungen.
After Table 14, Szondi states that the table can be used to interpret possible Mitte variations and then proceeds to examples.

sourceExcerpt: Auf Grund dieser Tabelle wird es nicht schwer sein, alle möglichen Mittevariationen zu deuten. Wir führen einige Beispiele an:
romanianRendering: Tabelele 13 și 14 funcționează ca hărți de referință pentru variațiile Mitte: configurațiile comune e/hy/k/p sunt puse în legătură cu exemple caracterologice, de socializare și cu tablouri patologice istorice, după care Szondi trece la exemple de interpretare.
doctrinalStatement: Analiza Mitte se face la nivelul configurației comune a celor patru factori e, hy, k și p. Tabelele 13–14 sunt atlasul sursei pentru variații caracterologice și psihopatologice și trebuie păstrate ca referință vizuală/contextuală. În registrul compact, ele nu justifică transformarea fiecărui rând într-o doctrină independentă și nici folosirea unei singure configurații ca diagnostic automat.
conditions: Use Tables 13 and 14 as source-defined configuration-level reference maps for Mitte interpretation.
Exact reaction signs and row associations remain governed by the admitted PDF tables.
exceptions: Do not serialize every table row as an independent doctrine merely because it appears in the source.
Do not modernize historical disease labels or treat table membership as a sufficient contemporary diagnosis.
Do not interpret e, hy, k or p in isolation when the table's unit of comparison is the joint Mitte configuration.
scopeNotes: Table 13, printed page 172, includes characterological variations and examples for socialization/pathology.
Table 14, printed pages 173–174, lists the source's historical 'kranke Mitte' configurations; it remains a primary-source lookup table for later targeted review.
The worked interpretations following Table 14 are examples, not separate doctrine unless they introduce a distinct rule or qualification.

relations.note: The tables operationalize the source's analysis of Mitte as a possible site of Triebgefahr.
Uses the source-defined four-factor Mitte structure e/hy/k/p.

ambiguities: Many reaction signs and several historical labels are OCR-sensitive; the admitted PDF tables are the visual authority.
reviewNotes: Canonical BODY U002497, U002499-U002501 and U002572 checked against deterministic P0 evidence; admitted PDF printed pages 172-174 visually verifies both tables.
High-compaction decision: the tables are retained as references rather than expanded into dozens of row-level doctrine records.
